summary: Black Drift duel: Varra answers a rival captain without a speech.
settingText: BLACK DRIFT HAVEN — OPEN SALVAGE GANTRY — NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: Rival Captain
dialogueInline.text: Queens belong in the Core.

dialogueInline.speaker: Varra Cindral
dialogueInline.text: Eat. Weld. Follow.

directionInline: A tumbling city of welded wrecks surrounds an asteroid. Forgefires spit into vacuum; oil-slick plating flashes bruised gold and violet. The rival sneers, Varra disarms him in one ugly-efficient movement and kicks him into a netted salvage pit. Hold on Varra as the watching crews erupt and engines spool up around the rock like answering throats.

summary: Varra's war deck: survival doctrine collides with Sira's appetite for spectacle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Varra Cindral
dialogueInline.text: We bleed their shields at the feeders. We do not torch farms. Flow keeps us breathing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sira Red Fang
dialogueInline.text: Flow is what's left after fire. Fire first.

dialogueInline.speaker: Elyra Vorn
dialogueInline.text: Or we live first.

directionInline: Captains crowd a crude map table made from engine cowling. Sira lounges feral; Elyra stays at the edge, watching everyone. Varra moves markers toward Auric Gate. Let the three women occupy the frame differently: Varra controlling space, Sira enjoying friction, Elyra measuring the cost.

summary: The Silent Triarch reduces a war to three brutal verbs.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raid Mask
dialogueInline.text: Strike to feed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Trade Mask
dialogueInline.text: Flow sustains.

dialogueInline.speaker: Fear Mask
dialogueInline.text: Terror binds.

directionInline: Three masked emissaries sit motionless in mismatched salvage thrones: Raid, Trade, Fear. Each speaks only once. Varra's jaw tightens; she accepts the words without bowing. The silence after them should feel like another vote.

summary: At Auric Bazaar, policy sounds different when spoken beside people who need heat.

dialogueInline.speaker: Governor Halev
dialogueInline.text: We need more than food. Medicine. Fuel cells. Heat. Lights for the out-rings.

dialogueInline.speaker: Elder Branth
dialogueInline.text: And fewer tariffs dressed as blessings.

dialogueInline.speaker: Captain Nira Sol
dialogueInline.text: You want safety? Ride formation and stop buying maps from raiders.

directionInline: Busy market life never stops around the argument: patched awnings, steaming food, cargo carts, mechanics carrying heater cores. Halev counts needs on his fingers. Branth chews a grain stem. Nira is all clipped military impatience.

summary: Halev chooses the green corridor because every alternative is worse.

dialogueInline.speaker: Elder Branth
dialogueInline.text: Maps that work are cheaper than escorts that don't.

dialogueInline.speaker: Governor Halev
dialogueInline.text: Enough. Essential cargo only. Fleet on the wing—if they'll take the terms.

directionInline: A child passes carrying a dead battery lantern while the men bargain over abstractions. Halev notices it, and that small sight ends the debate. He points toward the docks: decision made.

summary: The Admiralty argues whether a humanitarian lane is mercy or an exposed throat.

dialogueInline.speaker: Admiral Cael Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Blockades hold. Green corridors invite knives.

dialogueInline.speaker: Commodore Ilyra Venn
dialogueInline.text: Green lanes keep clinics stocked and heaters lit.

dialogueInline.speaker: Admiral Cyros Ven
dialogueInline.text: And strength looks like siege to civilians.

directionInline: Formal council glow, polished stone and projected corridor maps. Dominion remains physically above Venn on the dais. Solenne watches for weakness; Cyros watches the civilian numbers. Venn never raises her voice, which makes the disagreement sharper.

summary: Dominion permits the experiment without conceding the principle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Admiral Cael Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Hold the wall. Test their lane—under watch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Commodore Ilyra Venn
dialogueInline.text: Understood.

directionInline: Dominion's gaze lands on Venn. She gives one economical nod: not victory, not defeat. As she turns away, the green route remains glowing between them on the table.

summary: The Shards swear their war-moot with engines instead of words.
settingText: BLACK DRIFT HAVEN — EXTERIOR SALVAGE DECK — NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: Elyra Vorn
dialogueInline.text: The Core speaks in scrolls. The Verge in ledgers. The Shards—we swear with our engines.

directionInline: Dozens of ships ring the asteroid. One by one their engines flare in different colors and exhaust signatures until the whole haven becomes a brutal luminous chorus. Varra watches without smiling. Elyra's voice is quiet over the spectacle.

summary: The feint raid begins; Sira treats Varra's restraint like an insult.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sira Red Fang
dialogueInline.text: Fat ships coming. Light a tooth for luck.

directionInline: A skeletal truss slices through the Rift. Fast Shard skiffs form up precisely while the Ashfang Marauder hangs just outside formation like an animal refusing a leash. Sira grins into open comms.

summary: Venn refuses the bait and makes protection the tactical objective.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Confed pings entering feeder spine. Small, surgical.

dialogueInline.speaker: Commodore Ilyra Venn
dialogueInline.text: Hold formation. Civilians first. No hero chases.

directionInline: Vectors bloom across Venn's holo. Junior officers expect an attack order; instead she drags Thunderbreak's projected path between the raiders and the clinic ships. Show the crew recalibrating around her choice.

summary: Elyra quietly saves a clinic freighter while everyone else is looking for a fight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Elyra Vorn
dialogueInline.text: You're covered. Don't light your beacons.

directionInline: Elyra cold-drifts with engines dark. Outside, a medpod freighter spins toward exposed fire. She launches micro-tethers, catches it and reels it beneath debris shadow. Her crew exchanges looks: this was not the raid they came for.

summary: Sira breaks the plan because destruction is the point for her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sira Red Fang
dialogueInline.text: Look how they burn.

directionInline: Ashfang suddenly flares and strafes a storage spine. Thermal blankets and power cells tumble into vacuum and ignite in bright ugly sheets. The horror is specifically wasted warmth: heater cells burning while civilians need heat.

summary: Thunderbreak physically blocks Sira's firing lane rather than escalating the battle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Marauder off the leash.

dialogueInline.speaker: Commodore Ilyra Venn
dialogueInline.text: Interpose. Do not escalate.

directionInline: Thunderbreak rams a drifting structural beam sideways, its armored flank filling the frame between Ashfang and the clinic freighter. Sparks cascade across the hull like a meteor shower. Venn watches Sira's vector without blinking.

summary: Nira turns a frightened escort line into something that can hold.

dialogueInline.speaker: Captain Nira Sol
dialogueInline.text: On me! We're walking those clinic pods home.

directionInline: Nira grips the controls hard enough to whiten her knuckles. Her escorts wobble into position, then settle into a clean protective line around the medpods. Let the fear remain visible; competence does not erase it.

summary: Sira and Elyra leave the raid with opposite lessons.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sira Red Fang
dialogueInline.text: Next pass we don't miss.

dialogueInline.speaker: Elyra Vorn
dialogueInline.text: Next pass you hit your own shadow.

directionInline: Varra's skiffs disengage exactly on the mark. Ashfang turns slowly, predatory and furious. Gravefire slips past on a quieter vector. Elyra's line lands without heat; Sira has no answer for it.

summary: Jex sells Halev the thing institutions cannot quite provide: a workable compromise.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex Marrin
dialogueInline.text: You want a green lane? I can sell protection and silence. Both cost more than speeches.

dialogueInline.speaker: Governor Halev
dialogueInline.text: I want warmth in the outer rings and antiseptic in the clinics.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex Marrin
dialogueInline.text: Then you want me.

directionInline: Jex enters with anomaly-glass beads sewn into his cloak and a fresh bandage under one rib. Nira dislikes him immediately. Halev dislikes needing him more. Keep all three in the frame so every line has a reaction.

summary: Nira and Jex establish their relationship in four words each.

dialogueInline.speaker: Captain Nira Sol
dialogueInline.text: Or the Fleet. Preferably the Fleet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex Marrin
dialogueInline.text: Preferably profit. Preferably mine.

dialogueInline.speaker: Governor Halev
dialogueInline.text: No inspections. Rapid scans. You arbitrate disputes—for now.

directionInline: Jex smiles at 'for now' as if Halev just offered him a lifetime contract. Nira gives him a look that promises the opposite. Halev signs anyway.

summary: The first green corridor becomes a test of whether everyone can choose not to fire.

dialogueInline.speaker: Captain Nira Sol
dialogueInline.text: No one blinks. We do this and people sleep warm tonight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Commodore Ilyra Venn
dialogueInline.text: Thunderbreak standing by. Resolve holds.

directionInline: Green waypoints float through darkness. Freighters carry heater cores, medpods, fuel cells, infant formula and thermal blankets. Nira leads inside the lane; Thunderbreak shadows outside with weapons cold; Elyra ghosts at the edge. The tension is silence, not gunfire.

summary: Sira inches toward the convoy and discovers Varra can still stop her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sira Red Fang
dialogueInline.text: Green means go.

directionInline: Confed silhouettes drift in darkness, watching rather than striking. Ashfang creeps forward. A single hand signal flashes from Varra's shadowed skiff. Sira stares at it, furious, then throttles down.

summary: Jex runs the corridor from a back room and prepares to own either outcome.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex Marrin
dialogueInline.text: If anyone fires, you never heard of me. If no one fires, tell everyone it was me.

directionInline: Jex signs three slates at once while runners carry beacon codes, arbitration markers and bribe lists. His bandaged rib hurts when he laughs; he laughs anyway.

summary: The corridor's first anomaly appears and everyone has to resist shooting at a ghost.
settingText: GREEN CORRIDOR — MARKERS ONE AND TWO

dialogueInline.speaker: Captain Nira Sol
dialogueInline.text: Mark one clear. Mark two… clear. Keep breathing.

directionInline: A reflection ripple runs beside the convoy. For one breath a ghost freighter occupies the same lane as the real one, then fades. Fingers hover over triggers but nobody fires. Nira hears her own breathing in the headset.

summary: Venn marks a victory so small it sounds like a maintenance order.

dialogueInline.speaker: Commodore Ilyra Venn
dialogueInline.text: Lanterns lit at shift change.

directionInline: A junior officer finally exhales. Venn's shoulders ease by a fraction. She looks at the green icons crossing safely, then gives the order as if it were routine. The crew understands it is not.

summary: Halev watches icons become heaters, antibiotics and battery cells in his mind.

dialogueInline.speaker: Governor Halev
dialogueInline.text: Heaters. Antibiotics. Battery cells. All the small mercies.

directionInline: A cracked monitor reflects Halev's exhausted face while green cargo icons cross the last marker. Below him, dark apartment rings wait for power. He closes his eyes only after the final icon clears.

summary: Varra admits why she let the convoy pass; Elyra offers a different future.

dialogueInline.speaker: Elyra Vorn
dialogueInline.text: You let it pass.

dialogueInline.speaker: Varra Cindral
dialogueInline.text: We need clinics stocked when the next fire comes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Elyra Vorn
dialogueInline.text: Then let fewer fires come.

directionInline: Varra stands alone before the distant green pips. She never turns toward Elyra. Elyra does not press her. Engines thrum through the deck like held breath; the possibility of restraint hangs between them without being named.

summary: The convoy clears. Nira and Venn allow themselves one line of warmth.

dialogueInline.speaker: Captain Nira Sol
dialogueInline.text: Verge convoy to Thunderbreak—thanks for the shadow.

dialogueInline.speaker: Commodore Ilyra Venn
dialogueInline.text: Shadows are where lanterns matter most.

directionInline: The freighters peel toward Auric docks while escorts break formation. Nira smiles despite herself. On Thunderbreak, Venn says the line softly and immediately returns to work.

summary: Sira powers up, then chooses—barely—not to break the peace.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sira Red Fang
dialogueInline.text: Next time, little lanterns.

directionInline: Ashfang's engines flare hard enough to light the hulls around it. Sira grins, holds the burn for one dangerous second, then powers down. Make the restraint look more difficult for her than violence.

summary: Jex toasts the system he has just made himself indispensable to.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex Marrin
dialogueInline.text: Flow finds a way.

directionInline: Jex raises a glass to nobody. Outside, Veil Market neon buzzes and a distant beacon stutters. He drinks as new corridor orders begin arriving before the old ones have finished printing.
